scenes.setting: Cedar Lantern Terrace, the morning after the Amanagi finale. The lantern strings are still lit, the tea kiosk shutter is half open, and cars from all six crews fill the bays.

lines.speaker: narration
lines.line: By the time you park, the terrace is already full. Nobody has gone home to sleep.

lines.speaker: R01
lines.line: There you are! I saved you a cup. I also lost my gloves again, so it evens out.

lines.speaker: R02
lines.line: Same cup as the one I mended at Bellmaker. It came back whole. So did you.

lines.speaker: R08
lines.line: I watched the last sector twice on the replay. Repeatable. That's all I ever wanted to see.

lines.speaker: R16
lines.line: You read that road the way you'd read weather. Nothing on it was random. Well done.

lines.speaker: R24
lines.line: I measured your run against hers. Hers was perfect. Yours left room for everybody. I've changed my notes.

lines.speaker: R32
lines.line: Composed, with the whole mountain watching. I told you it was harder than winning.

scenes.setting: The timing board beside the tea kiosk. Every convoy driver's slip from Amanagi is pinned in a row, and Reina Kurogane is standing in front of it.

lines.speaker: R40
lines.line: Every slip is different. Different lines, different mistakes. And the result is still yours, together.

lines.speaker: R40
lines.line: I thought sharing a result would dilute it. It doesn't, does it. Each of you is still on there.

lines.speaker: R34
lines.line: She's been standing here for twenty minutes. That's how Reina says 'I was wrong'.

lines.speaker: R40
lines.line: Thank you, Chika. I'm quite capable of saying it myself. ...I was wrong. About part of it.

lines.speaker: R40
lines.line: I'll keep driving alone some nights. But not because I can't trust anyone. That was never the reason.

lines.speaker: R40
lines.line: There's someone I should call. Not today. Soon.

scenes.setting: The radio bench at dusk. The receiver is on, the kettle is on, and cars are starting to leave for the evening roads.

lines.speaker: R19
lines.line: I pinned a copy of the old slip up here too. The last sector's still blank. Somebody knows why.

lines.speaker: R42
lines.line: Somebody always does. Leave it on the board. The frequency has a long memory.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.line: This is the Night Signal. Congratulations to {convoy}. Roads reopen at dusk. Everyone's welcome.

lines.speaker: narration
lines.line: The series goes on. Every road, every rival and every slip on the board is still yours to chase.

scenes.setting: The Amanagi Dawnline finish, above the sea. The mist has cleared on schedule and the sun is just over the horizon. A timing-crew van is parked at the final sector post.

lines.speaker: timing-crew
lines.line: Sector five, descent to the sea: recorded. Final time: recorded. Every sector, every car.

lines.speaker: R48
lines.line: Recorded. Well. That only took eighteen years and a very good convoy.

lines.speaker: R47
lines.line: The car's fine. Better than fine. You didn't waste a single degree of those tyres.

lines.speaker: R48
lines.line: Neither did you, {convoy}. That's the part I'll remember. The time is just the proof.

lines.speaker: narration
lines.line: Far below, the first train of the morning runs along the coast. It sounds its horn twice.

lines.speaker: R46
lines.line: That's my old line. Somebody in the cab still knows the signal. Ha. Right on time.

scenes.setting: Cedar Lantern Terrace, mid-morning. Shiori Kuze is sitting at the radio bench with the old receiver. Her cream scarf, mended in two places, is folded beside her.

lines.speaker: R48
lines.line: Sit down, please. You've earned the ending, and it's shorter than the legend.

lines.speaker: R48
lines.line: The relay clock at the last sector died in the cold. The volunteer timer was sixteen and frozen to the bone.

lines.speaker: R48
lines.line: So I stopped. I gave her my scarf, and we restarted the clock together. The run was over. I didn't mind.

lines.speaker: R40
lines.line: I minded. I was the timer. I thought I'd cost you the only run that mattered.

lines.speaker: R48
lines.line: You were the only part of that morning that mattered, Reina. You returned the scarf torn. I mended it.

lines.speaker: R40
lines.line: ...I stopped depending on anyone after that. I told myself it was discipline.

lines.speaker: R48
lines.line: It was discipline. It was also lonely. You can keep the first and put the second down.

scenes.setting: The radio bench, later. The timing crew has brought the old carbon slip from the Floodmark archive, and today's slip beside it.

lines.speaker: timing-crew
lines.line: We could copy today's fifth sector onto the old slip. Close the story properly.

lines.speaker: R48
lines.line: Leave the old one blank. That morning's answer wasn't a number. Pin today's next to it instead.

lines.speaker: R42
lines.line: Then that's what I'll say on air. Nothing embellished. Just both slips, side by side.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.line: This is the Night Signal. The Amanagi dawn run has been timed. The old slip stays as it was.

lines.speaker: R48
lines.line: I'll be here most mornings, if the kettle's on. The road will be there too. Come and use it well.

postGameNote: The Night Signal keeps broadcasting. Campaign replay, Freeplay, ghosts, customisation, Cedar Lantern Terrace and every remaining challenge stay open, including the reference trial at the old timing cabin on Four Signals Traverse. Your garage, wallet, convoy and progress carry on. There is no New Game, because there's nothing to start over.
